topic: You Probably Don't Need a Vector Database for RAG: Simpler Alternatives That Work (2026)

key_points: BM25 keyword search achieves 88% recall@10 vs 91.7% for OpenAI embeddings on SQuAD — negligible practical difference
Hybrid approach (BM25 top-50 reranked by embeddings) outperforms pure vector search
Classical IR methods (reverse indexes, TF-IDF, BM25) are well-established, scalable, and don't need vector DB infrastructure
Vector databases add cost and complexity without meaningful accuracy gains for most RAG use cases
Roaming RAG uses SQLite FTS5 for keyword retrieval instead of vector embeddings
Eliminates embedding pipeline costs and vector DB maintenance
Works well for domain-specific content where terminology is precise and keyword matching is effective
Demonstrates that many RAG applications don't need semantic search
StarRocks built 'Rocky' — a RAG Slack assistant using SQL retrieval and one OLAP table
Uses Gemini for LLM, SQL-based retrieval instead of vector search
Eliminates separate vector DB by leveraging existing OLAP infrastructure
Proves enterprise RAG can work without dedicated vector infrastructure
PageIndex uses hierarchical tree-based document indexing instead of vector embeddings
Reasoning-based RAG uses tree search (inspired by AlphaGo) for structured document retrieval
Achieves better retrieval accuracy than vector-based systems for professional/financial documents
Nodes align with document sections preserving context — no arbitrary chunking needed
Production RAG costs $2,400/month for 50 queries/day — vector DB is 40-50% of the bill
Token-aware context assembly (3.2K tokens vs 12K) saves 35% with same accuracy
Hybrid reranking (70% semantic + 30% keyword) reduces top-20 to top-8 while maintaining quality
Embedding caching with 45-60% intra-day hit rate saves 20% on API costs

stats.fact: Beyond 3,000 tokens of context, RAG accuracy plateaus — everything beyond is noise and cost
Token-aware context assembly (3.2K vs 12K tokens) saves 35% with identical accuracy
Embedding caching achieves 45-60% intra-day hit rate, saving 20% on API costs
Hybrid reranking (70% semantic + 30% keyword) reduces retrieval from top-20 to top-8 while maintaining quality
SQLite FTS5 provides production-grade full-text search with zero additional infrastructure cost
stats.source: SQLite documentation and Roaming RAG case study

stats.fact: PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector) is production-ready and used by Omni for workplace search at scale
stats.source: Omni (getomnico/omni) — open-source workplace search on Postgres

angles: Vector databases are overkill for most RAG applications — classical IR methods match or exceed their performance at a fraction of the cost
The hybrid approach (BM25 + embedding reranking) is the sweet spot: use cheap keyword search for initial retrieval, then rerank with vectors on a small subset
SQLite FTS5 and PostgreSQL tsvector are production-ready alternatives that eliminate vector DB infrastructure entirely
Reasoning-based RAG (tree search, PageIndex) outperforms vector similarity for domain-specific documents
Cost optimization: most RAG pipelines waste 40-50% on vector DB costs that could be eliminated with simpler alternatives
